title: Adaptive Phase Tessellation & Kernel Affinity Scheduler for Prefill/Decode
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Current prefill/decode arbitration treats long prefill requests as monolithic phases which hurts latency for mixed workloads and prevents fine-grained kernel affinity decisions. Goal: implement a scheduler that tessellates long prefill sequences into variable-length microphases ("micro-tessellation") driven by attention-cost heuristics and kernel-affinity signals. The scheduler should: 1) dynamically split prefill into microphases where each microphase has a predicted attention cost and preferred kernel (fp16/quantized/sparse-aware); 2) schedule microphases respecting tenant SLOs and fair share windows; 3) surface metrics to the Console (per-microphase latency, kernel switch overhead, fairness deltas). Acceptance criteria: end-to-end 95th latency improvement for short interactive requests when co-located with long prefills (target: 20% reduction), no >2% regression in throughput for batch-dominant tenants, coherent kernel selection signal delivered to runtime with <0.5ms decision latency. Out-of-scope for this ticket: new kernel implementations themselves and persistent KV cache changes. Deliverables: design doc, simulation harness, canary in prod with two tenants, dashboard widgets, and a follow-up PR with opt-in flag. Trade-offs: finer tessellation improves responsiveness but increases kernel-switch overhead and fragmentation of batching opportunities. We'll explore a cost model that balances attention compute saved vs kernel-switch penalty. Metrics: latency p50/p95/p99 per tenant, kernel switch rate, microphase length distribution, batch occupancy, token/sec. Rollout plan: local simulation -> internal perf cluster A/B -> opt-in canary on runtime-1.22 for selected customers -> gradual ramp. Risks: inaccurate attention-cost predictor causing harmful splits; increased scheduler CPU overhead; telemetry volume. Proposed mitigations: start conservative (min microphase length 8 tokens), RL-grade estimator gated behind a fallback heuristic, throttle kernel switches per-device. References: Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Adaptive+Tessellation (draft), perf-sim repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prefill-sim, related infra tickets ENG-271828, ENG-325901.
